newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian state has final say in gaming permit.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian state has final say in gaming permit.

text.p: Malaysia's eastern Sabah state has the final say in allowing Olympia Industries Bhd's gaming unit to operate its lottery services in the state, Deputy Finance Minister Affifudin Omar said on Thursday.

The national Bernama news agency quoted Affifudin as saying: "Though the ministry has fulfilled the company's request to renew its gaming licence which was previously revoked, the final decision is on the state government."
He said it was up to the Sabah state authorities to give the business premises licence which Olympia's subsidiary Diriwan Corp Sdn Bhd would need to carry on its lottery operations.

"It is the right of the Sabah state government to have such a stand. We (the ministry), only renew the gaming licence, but to operate the business depends on the state government's permission," added Affifudin.
Olympia had said on Tuesday that the Ministry of Finance had agreed to renew the gaming licence for it to conduct lottery games effective from January 1, 1997.
However, on Wednesday, the Sabah chief minister said his government did not plan to renew that licence.
Diriwan's gaming licence, which was held by Lotteries Corp Sdn Bhd, was revoked on January 4, 1996, resulting in the closure of all its gaming outlets.

Shares of Olympia remained suspended on Thursday pending an announcement of a proposed takeover, while parent company Mycom Bhd closed 22 cents lower to 3.36 ringgit. Mycom owns a 54.7 percent stake in Olympia.
